## Purpose
Each `useXxx.ts` file under `src/hooks/**` wraps exactly one TanStack Query concern around a `lib/*.ts` fetch wrapper — never a raw `call()`. The three exemplars (`useArtifactDrift`, `useEconomySummary`, `useFileContent`) show the two shapes this subproject repeats everywhere: a single-item `useQuery` gated by `enabled: !!param`, and a per-project fan-out via `useQueries` keyed by `p.path`. A short header comment states what backend command the hook wraps, why the query is disabled/enabled the way it is, and any fail-open/staleTime reasoning a future editor would otherwise have to rediscover.

## Convention
Folder: apps/dashboard/src/hooks/** · Extension: .ts · Files of this role in this subproject: 20
`queryKey` is always an array literal whose leaves are the params the query actually varies on (`repoPath`, `spec`, a derived stable string), never an object. Every query that depends on an optional value sets `enabled: !!value` rather than guarding inside `queryFn` (so a missing param never fires a request) and casts the value with `as string` inside `queryFn` — the standard "gated-then-asserted" idiom in this codebase. `staleTime` is set explicitly and its cadence is justified in a comment (`60_000` for slow-moving drift, `5_000`/`30_000` for watcher-driven data, `refetchInterval` only when explicitly polling a live cadence). Fan-out hooks use `useQueries` keyed by the entity's own identity field (`p.path`), never by array index, and re-zip results back onto the source array by iterating it again — not by assuming index alignment survives a re-render.

## How to apply
A new hook is a new `src/hooks/useXxx.ts` file, one hook (plus at most one small sibling variant, e.g. a `-Single` companion) per file, importing its fetch function from the matching `lib/*.ts` wrapper — never calling `call()` inline. Name the file and the exported function identically (`useFoo.ts` exports `useFoo`). If the hook fans a query out per project, follow `useArtifactDrift`/`useProjectDetections`: read the project list from `useProjectsStore`, build the `useQueries` array, then re-map results into a `Record`/array aligned back onto the source list.

## Examples
Ref: apps/dashboard/src/hooks/useFileContent.ts
```ts
export function useFileContent(repoPath: string | null, relPath: string | null) {
  return useQuery<FileContent>({
    queryKey: ["read-file", repoPath, relPath],
    queryFn: () => fetchReadFile(repoPath as string, relPath as string),
    enabled: !!repoPath && !!relPath,
    staleTime: 30_000,
  });
}
```

Ref: apps/dashboard/src/hooks/useArtifactDrift.ts
```ts
export function useArtifactDrift(): Record<string, ArtifactDriftRow> {
  const projects = useProjectsStore((s) => s.projects);

  const queries = useQueries({
    queries: projects.map((p) => ({
      queryKey: ["artifact-drift", p.path],
      queryFn: () => artifactUpdateCheck(p.path),
      staleTime: 60_000,
      retry: false,
    })),
  });
```

Ref: apps/dashboard/src/hooks/useEconomySummary.ts
```ts
export function useEconomySummary(
  scope: EconomyScope | null,
  period: EconomyWindowPeriod,
): UseQueryResult<EconomySummary> {
  return useQuery<EconomySummary>({
    queryKey: ["economy-summary", scope && stableScopeKey(scope), period],
    queryFn: () => fetchEconomySummary(scope as EconomyScope, economyWindow(period)),
    enabled: !!scope,
```
